In **ascending order**, the values of $t$ at which the curve $x=t+4,\,y=\frac{1}{2}{t}^{2}-3$ intersects the line $y=\frac{1}{2}x-2$ (shown above) are

question.worked_solution:
Notice that the line and curve intersect twice, so we expect two solutions.

To find the coordinates of the intersection points, we take the equation of the line, replace $x$ and $y$ with the parametric formulas, and then solve for $t.$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}y & =\frac{1}{2}x-2 \\ \frac{1}{2}{t}^{2}-3 & =\frac{1}{2}(t+4)-2 \\ {t}^{2}-6 & =(t+4)-4 \\ {t}^{2}-6 & =t \\ {t}^{2}-t-6 & =0 \\ (t+2)(t-3) & =0 \\ t & =-2,\,3.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, in ascending order, the values of $t$ where the curve $x=t+4,\,y=\frac{1}{2}{t}^{2}-3$ intersects the line $y=\frac{1}{2}x-2$ are $t=-2$ and $t=3.$
